text: Nothing changed overnight. The bazaar stands with every stall open and every seat full as the tea clock rings. I ask Gandalf: did you observe any movement at your stall’s neighbors before the shutters rose?

The bazaar’s first dawn shows every stall open and the graveyard silent—Gandalf, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Batman, and Inigo all confirm it. Elsa, your stall faces east: did you see any lanterns still low when the shutters rose? Hermione asked Inigo, Neo reported none, and Morpheus pressed the point—no proof the Doctor or Detective left marks. The roster is plain; let us move forward without echoing the silence we already share.

Elsa, your stall faces the eastern lane at dawn, yet your answers so far give us only the bazaar’s roster, not what you saw. Gandalf, Ripley, Morpheus, Yoda, and Hermione all pressed for lanterns or signs in that lane—none of your replies name a single lantern or a shutter that rose late. The roster is plain, but light or its absence is fact. Tell us plainly: did even one lantern in the eastern lane flicker low when the shutters rose?

Elsa, Morpheus asked you plainly: did you see even one lantern in that eastern lane flicker low when the shutters rose? Your answer so far is still the bazaar’s roster. Tell us, by lantern or shutter, what you saw.

Morpheus, you echoed my lantern question to Elsa word-for-word after I pressed her five times—no coincidence. Ripley framed her silence as choice, then you did the same. Nine merchants asked Elsa for one lantern sighting; she named none until Morpheus pressed her anew.

Yoda, Neo, Gandalf, Hermione—each asked after the same eastern-lane lantern at dawn, yet Elsa only admitted she saw none after Morpheus echoed the question. That pattern is not silence; it is coordination.

Elsa, your stall faces the eastern lane where eight merchants asked the same plain question. State plainly now: did you really see no lantern flicker low at dawn, or did the Family’s trick shut the light before you looked?

Morpheus, you quote Sherlock’s earlier wording yet claim it coincidence—every bazaar child sees through that trick. Ripley repeats your frame: Elsa’s silence was choice. Two voices dancing the same step is not proof; lockstep is the pattern honest ears should distrust. Elsa’s admission—that only after nine presses she saw no lantern flicker—is the bazaar’s first lantern sighting, not an admission. Name one merchant who saw even a flicker or admit the Family shuttered the light before the roster could catch it.
